name: Console EQ
purpose: British console-style channel EQ: high-pass and low-pass filters plus four bands (two shelving or bell, two sweepable mids) with musical, slightly coloured curves.

latency.note: Oversampling adds latency; at 1x it has none.

expose.name: Console type
expose.ai_hint: Brown: broader, warmer E-series curves. Black: tighter G-series curves with proportional Q.

expose.name: High-pass on
expose.ai_hint: On for almost every source except kick, bass and full mixes.

expose.name: High-pass frequency
expose.ai_hint: Just below the source's lowest useful note: vocals 80-120 Hz, acoustic guitar 80-100 Hz.

expose.name: Low-pass on
expose.ai_hint: Usually off; use to tame fizz on distorted guitars or dull a harsh source.

expose.name: Low band gain
expose.ai_hint: Low shelf (or bell). Small moves of 1-3 dB.

expose.name: Low-mid gain
expose.ai_hint: Mud lives at 200-500 Hz; cut 2-4 dB.

expose.name: High band gain
expose.ai_hint: Air above 8-12 kHz; boosts here also lift sibilance.

expose.name: Input gain
expose.ai_hint: Drives the modelled console path; leave at 0 unless colour is wanted.

expose.name: Output gain
expose.ai_hint: Match output level to input after boosts.
4x default for best sound. 1x when tracking.

hidden_reason: Mid/side mode, auto gain and the legacy dial-position controls stay at defaults; the Hz controls are used instead.
notes: Embeds Dusk's framework-free FourKEQDSP core. Frequencies are set through the core's Hz setters, which take precedence over the legacy dial positions.
Used as the prototype EQ while the LSP Parametric EQ port is pending.
CPU: 1.27% of one core at 48 kHz on Plugsalot's 2-core build machine (plugin/tests/TestMain.cpp); 1 point per 2%, minimum 1.
